title.en: Analyse the four cases of simultaneous shifts
Identify which variable changes definitely and which is indeterminate

say.en: In summer, demand for ice-cream rises, and dairies also produce more. Will the price rise or fall? Sometimes the honest answer is: it depends. In this lesson: Analyse the four cases of simultaneous shifts.
Identify which variable changes definitely and which is indeterminate.

body.en: When demand and supply shift together, one of price or quantity changes in a definite direction and the other depends on the relative size of the *shifts*. (1) Both increase: quantity rises; price may rise, fall or stay the same. (2) Both decrease: quantity falls; price is indeterminate. (3) Demand increases, supply decreases: price rises; quantity is indeterminate. (4) Demand decreases, supply increases: price falls; quantity is indeterminate.

points.en: Same direction: quantity definite, price indeterminate
Opposite directions: price definite, quantity indeterminate

narration.en: When both curves shift in the same direction, quantity changes for sure and price is uncertain. When they shift in opposite directions, price changes for sure and quantity is uncertain.
narration.kn: ಎರಡೂ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಿದರೆ ಪ್ರಮಾಣದ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಖಚಿತ, ಬೆಲೆ ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ. ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಿದರೆ ಬೆಲೆಯ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಖಚಿತ, ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ.

say.en: When both curves shift in the same direction, quantity changes for sure and price is uncertain. When they shift in opposite directions, price changes for sure and quantity is uncertain. Same direction: quantity definite, price indeterminate.
say.kn: ಎರಡೂ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಿದರೆ ಪ್ರಮಾಣದ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಖಚಿತ, ಬೆಲೆ ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ. ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಿದರೆ ಬೆಲೆಯ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಖಚಿತ, ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ.

say.en: Opposite directions: price definite, quantity indeterminate.
Let us draw a table with four rows: the four ways demand and supply can shift together.
Same direction: both up means quantity surely rises; both down means quantity surely falls. Price depends on which shift is bigger.
Opposite directions: demand up and supply down surely raise price; demand down and supply up surely lower it. Quantity depends.

title.en: Using numbers to settle the ambiguity

body.en: The indeterminate change can be found only when we know the size of the shifts. With $q^D = 300 + d - 10p$ and $q^S = 50 + s + 15p$, the equilibrium price is $p^* = (250 + d - s)/25$. If d = s, price does not change; if d > s, price rises; if d < s, price falls.

points.en: Equal shifts: price unchanged (both ↑) or quantity unchanged (opposite)
Bigger shift decides the indeterminate variable

narration.en: To know the uncertain change, we need the sizes of the shifts. If demand shifts more than supply, price rises; if less, price falls.
narration.kn: ಅನಿಶ್ಚಿತ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ತಿಳಿಯಲು ಸರಿತಗಳ ಗಾತ್ರ ಬೇಕು. ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸರಿದರೆ ಬೆಲೆ ಏರುತ್ತದೆ; ಕಡಿಮೆ ಸರಿದರೆ ಇಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: qD = 300 − 10p, qS = 50 + 15p (equilibrium ₹10, 200). Find the new equilibrium if (a) demand and supply both rise by 50 units at every price; (b) demand rises by 50 and supply by 100.

steps.en: In both cases quantity rises, as expected when both curves shift right; the price change depends on the sizes.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. qD = 300 − 10p, qS = 50 + 15p (equilibrium ₹10, 200). Find the new equilibrium if (a) demand and supply both rise by 50 units at every price; (b) demand rises by 50 and supply by 100.

say.en: Let us work this out together. qD equals 300 minus 10p, qS equals 50 plus 15p (equilibrium 10, rupees 200). Find the new equilibrium if a demand and supply both rise by 50 units at every price; b demand rises by 50 and supply by 100.
a 350 minus 10p equals 100 plus 15p gives 25p equals 250 gives p equals 10 rupees unchanged; q equals 350 minus 100 equals 250 up by 50.
b 350 minus 10p equals 150 plus 15p gives 25p equals 200 gives p equals 8 rupees falls; q equals 350 minus 80 equals 270 up by 70.
In both cases quantity rises, as expected when both curves shift right; the price change depends on the sizes.
So the answer is a 10, rupees 250 units; b 8, rupees 270 units.

heading.en: Same sure Quantity, Opposite sure Price

body.en: If the curves move the Same way, Quantity is sure. If they move Opposite ways, Price is sure.
